methods.label: Use the identity at reciprocal inputs
methods.explanation:
The identity contains both \(f(x)\) and \(f(1/x)\). Replacing \(x\) by \(1/x\) exchanges these two quantities, giving a second equation we can use to eliminate one of them. This substitution is valid whenever \(x\ne0\).

The two equations are
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(x)+2f(1/x)&=3x,\\
2f(x)+f(1/x)&=3/x.
\end{aligned}
\]
Double the second equation and subtract the first to obtain
\[
3f(x)=\frac6x-3x,
\qquad f(x)=\frac2x-x.
\]
This rule satisfies the original identity, since
\[
\left(\frac2x-x\right)+2\left(2x-\frac1x\right)=3x.
\]
For every nonzero \(x\),
\[
f(-x)=-\frac2x+x=-f(x).
\]
Thus \(f(x)=f(-x)\) holds exactly when \(f(x)=0\). Since \(x\ne0\),
\[
\frac2x-x=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x^2=2.
\]
The two solutions are \(x=\sqrt2\) and \(x=-\sqrt2\). Both are nonzero, so exactly two real numbers satisfy the equation, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
